items.summary: As MLAs prepare to return to historic Province House for the fall sitting of P.E.I.’s legislature next week, the governing Progressive Conservatives are facing serious questions about their political fundraising.

items.title: France promises to replace its university admissions system after riots and thousands of arrests
items.summary: France’s government pledged Monday to replace its national online university admissions platform by 2028, seeking to quell student anger after weeks of often violent mass protests over education and living costs.

items.title: E-scooter rider fired multiple pellets at pedestrians walking Toronto trail, police say
items.summary: Toronto police are looking for an e-scooter rider who they said shot pellets at pedestrians along a trail last week.

items.title: Canada’s longest-serving mayor vying for 15th consecutive term
items.summary: Canada’s longest-serving mayor is seeking re-election on Monday after more than four decades in office. Gord Krantz has been the mayor of Milton, Ont. since 1980, serving 14 consecutive terms – longer than any other mayor in Canada.

items.title: Man found dead in Queensland floods named as former councillor and One Nation candidate
items.summary: Fraser coast mayor described James Hansen as ‘always ready to help others, contribute to the community and advocate strongly’

items.title: Ontario legislature returning after 21 weeks with new faces, rejigged cabinet, cloud of scandal
items.summary: Provincial politicians are returning to the Ontario legislature Tuesday after a long break. The spotlight in question period is expected to largely focus on the Ford government's handling of Ontario Student Assistance Program payments to career colleges.

items.title: Southeast Asia’s housing paradox: too many homes, too few buyers
items.summary: In parts of Southeast Asia, unsold homes are piling up as developers struggle to clear housing stock – yet young buyers hoping to land their first property still cannot find an affordable home.
